title: Verifier limit: bytecode counting cannot see C-level builtin work

body.signal: A candidate that shifts work from Python bytecode into C builtins (str methods, dict ops, itertools) scores an 'improvement' that the instruction counter manufactured.
body.failure_mode: Instruction counting is deterministic and reproducible but structurally blind below the bytecode layer; phase0's largest passing 'improvement' was driven by exactly this shift (word_cooccurrence family).
body.detection: When a large claimed gain coincides with replacing Python-level loops with builtin calls, cross-check with wall-clock timing on the held-out workload before trusting it.
body.fix_strategy: Disclose the metric limit in every benchmark report (as phase0 does); where affordable, pair op counts with timing on a fixed machine profile.

provenance.note: Seeded from hand-authored/analyzed artifacts; promoted by human decision, not agent replay.
